subject: Cascade AI: priority SLO approval + product clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@cascade.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Patricia Lopez <patricia.lopez@cascade.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Priority SLO for Cascade AI (P95 75ms)

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Cascade AI is moving fast and they asked if Redwood can commit to a P95 response time of 75ms for their highest-priority route (short chat queries, ~256 tokens). They understand this is outside standard terms and are open to a temporary premium/commitment.

Attached is a short SLO request doc and a usage histogram for their production traffic (see CascadeAI_SLO_Request_v2.pdf). Key asks:
- P95 <= 75ms for priority route (~20% of their qps)
- 99.95% uptime for that route
- Support hours: 24x7 on-call during rollout window (first 30 days)

Can you confirm if Redwood can evaluate and what product/ops asks we should expect?

—Alex
Alex Taylor
Head of Platform
Cascade AI

Subject: Fwd: Request: Priority SLO for Cascade AI (P95 75ms)

Folks — forwarding Cascade's ask. Summary: P95 75ms for short-chat route, 99.95% uptime, 24x7 on-call for rollout. Cascade is a strategic account; sales/legal are ready to offer committed spend.

Product questions I have (need answers to feed back to Alex):
1) Is P95 75ms realistic for ~256-token interactive requests on our current infra if we pin them to dedicated instances/quantized model variant?
2) What operational guarantees do we need to include (prefix caching, dedicated pool size, fallback behavior)?
3) What does the rollback plan look like if latencies spike during rollout?

Ops: Dylan — can you sketch what a 24x7 coverage plan for the first 30 days would look like and what SRE ramp is required?

Legal/Sales: once product/ops confirms feasibility, we'll need a short commitment doc (one-page) and a DocuSign for signatures. I've attached the customer's request for reference.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Priority SLO for Cascade AI (P95 75ms)

Jasmine —

Short answer: potentially doable with constraints. Quick notes after an initial runbook review:
- Model: Must pin to a lower-latency quantized variant (q4f/8) tailored for short-context if they accept a small trade-off in top-n sampling quality.
- Dedicated pool: Recommend a dedicated pool sized to their 95th percentile concurrency + 25% buffer. Based on their histogram, that's ~48 concurrent workers.
- Caching: KV/prefix caching for repeated prefixes will be critical. We need to enable sticky routing for priority route.
- Fallback: If latency exceeds threshold, traffic should degrade to a higher-latency but higher-throughput variant (same model family) — this must be explicit in the commitment.

Operational asks for the SLA document:
- Warm-up run: 72h soak in staging with synthetic traffic mirroring their histogram.
- Monitoring: per-route latency SLO with 30s alerting and a rolling 1h mitigation SLA for on-call.
- Capacity escalation: automatic burst pool to absorb +30% qps for 2 hours.

I'll put a short technical appendix for the commitment (what we can guarantee vs what is advisory). If legal needs precise phrasing for fallbacks, loop Ben and I'll mark hard vs advisory language.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Product Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Priority SLO for Cascade AI (P95 75ms)

Agree with Marcus. Ops notes and cost/effort estimate below:
- Staffing: dedicated on-call rotation for 30 days: 2x primary engineers (12-hour shift overlap) + 1 escalation lead. Estimate 0.5 FTE during ramp, then revert to standard duty.
- Runbook diffs: attaching an ops-runbook-diff.txt that enumerates required runbook changes (traffic-class routing, cache priming, alert thresholds).
- Infra cost: dedicated pool + burst capacity increases monthly cost estimate by ~32% for the routes covered. We can present this as a line-item in a commitment.
- Rollback: automated weighted traffic shift back to hosted pool with circuit-breaker after 5 consecutive 95th-percentile breaches in 10 minutes.

Next steps: Marcus to finalise the tech appendix and we should get legal to sign off on fallback language. Jasmine — can you confirm the commercial uplift Cascade is prepared to commit to?

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Cloud Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Jasmine / Marcus —

Representing Cascade AI for the legal/procurement side. Cascade can move fast on signatures if we deliver clear language on:
1) Scope of the priority route (explicit route identifier and traffic class).
2) Clear fallback and mitigation clauses (they want to avoid silent silent degradations).
3) A 30-day trial window with a mutual review and exit clauses (30 days notice).

I've attached a short redline summary in the DocuSign packet. Procurement will require a single PO and they want billing to be monthly with the committed premium applied. I'll be ready to route signatures once product/ops confirm the appendix text.

—Ben O'Rourke
VentureLaw LLP (external counsel for Cascade AI)
